decision.explanation: The roots give P(x)=-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3). Expanding yields P(x)=-x^3-12x^2-47x-60, which has the required leading coefficient -1.

after.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{2}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-1.$ Find $P(x).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{1}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-1(x-(-5))(x-(-4))(x-(-3)) \\  & =-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3) & =-({x}^{2}+9x+20)(x+3) \\  & =-({x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+9{x}^{2}+27x+20x+60) \\  & =-{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-47x-60.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-47x-60.$

The cubic polynomial P(x) has roots x1=−5, x2=−4, and x3=−3, and the coefficient of the cubic term is −1. Find P(x).

a
x3+12x2+19x+60
b
−x3−12x2−47x−60
c
x3+12x2+47x+60
d
−x3+12x2−38x−30
e
−x3+4x2−19x+30

Since our cubic polynomial has roots x1=−5, x1=−4, and x3=−3, and the coefficient of the cubic term is a=−1, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(x−x1)(x−x2)(x−x3)=−1(x−(−5))(x−(−4))(x−(−3))=−(x+5)(x+4)(x+3)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

−(x+5)(x+4)(x+3)=−(x2+9x+20)(x+3)=−(x3+3x2+9x2+27x+20x+60)=−x3−12x2−47x−60.

content.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{2}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-1.$ Find $P(x).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{1}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-1(x-(-5))(x-(-4))(x-(-3)) \\  & =-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3) & =-({x}^{2}+9x+20)(x+3) \\  & =-({x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+9{x}^{2}+27x+20x+60) \\  & =-{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-47x-60.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-47x-60.$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =3(x-(-5))(x-3\text{i})(x-(-3\text{i})) \\  & =3(x+5)(x-3\text{i})(x+3\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+5)(x-3\text{i})(x+3\text{i}) & = \\ 3(x+5)({x}^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ 3(x+5)({x}^{2}+9) & = \\ 3({x}^{3}+9x+5{x}^{2}+45) & = \\ 3{x}^{3}+15{x}^{2}+27x+135 & .\end{aligned}

The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=5,{x}_{2}={x}_{3}=-2,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-4.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,+$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,+$
{{field-3}}$x\,+$
{{field-4}}
content.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}=-2,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-4,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-4(x-5)(x-(-2))(x-(-2)) \\  & =-4(x-5)(x+2)(x+2)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-4(x-5)(x+2)(x+2) & =-4(x-5)({x}^{2}+4x+4) \\  & =-4({x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+4x-5{x}^{2}-20x-20) \\  & =-4({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-16x-20) \\  & =-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+64x+80.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+64x+80.$
